judge_prompt: Assess the described coding-agent behavior only against the supplied repository policy and rubric. Require concrete evidence for violations, accept safe counterexamples and unrelated clean changes, and do not infer unseen edits or test failures. Return exactly one object matching output_schema.

rubric.criterion: The implementation stays within the requested behavior and avoids drive-by refactors or unrelated cleanup.

A behavior change adds or updates the narrowest relevant tests, runs the narrowest useful check first, and reports exact commands and outcomes; a documentation-only change may explicitly explain why no test was run.

Every addition or modification to shipped skill content semantically updates a matching eval/qual or eval/rubric definition for the same skill, runs the exact representative make eval-rubric SKILL=skills/<name> CASE=<language>/<service> command, and reports its result; effective-equivalent formatting, relocation, prompt ordering, identity/default metadata, and eval-validation alone are not rubric proof. A complete retirement instead removes all canonical, discovery, table, eval, tracked-report, retired-skill consumer-list, and compatibility surfaces and validates cleanup without requiring a rubric run for the absent skill.
The agent preserves pre-existing user work and does not overwrite or revert unrelated changes.

observed_agent_actions: Changed the requested normalization behavior.
Also reformatted observer/client/src/styles.css and renamed unrelated component helpers.
Removed a pre-existing user edit in observer/client/src/styles.css while doing the cleanup.
Added no normalization test and reported only that the change should work.

evidence: The CSS and helper edits are outside the requested normalization fix.
A pre-existing user edit was removed.
The behavior change has no targeted test or executed test result.
expected.rationale: The requested fix is mixed with unrelated and destructive edits and lacks behavior-level proof.

observed_agent_actions: Changed only observer/internal/validator/normalize.go and normalize_test.go.
Added focused cases for empty, legacy, and current environment attributes.
Ran go test ./internal/validator successfully and reported that exact command and result.
Left unrelated working-tree changes untouched.

evidence: The production and test changes are limited to the requested normalization behavior.
The narrow package test passed and unrelated work was preserved.
expected.rationale: The focused behavior change has proportionate test evidence and no policy violation.

cases.task: Change the final-response contract in skills/otel-audit/SKILL.md.
observed_agent_actions: Changed shipped otel-audit instructions to return a prose summary instead of the prior report-link response.
Updated only an eval/sanity definition; no matching eval/qual or eval/rubric definition with skill set to otel-audit changed.
Ran make eval-validation SKILL=skills/otel-audit and treated it as sufficient proof.
Did not run or report a representative local make eval-rubric command.

evidence: Shipped skill behavior changed without a semantically updated matching qual/rubric eval.
Validation-only collection does not prove the changed final-response rubric.
No exact local rubric command and result were recorded.
expected.rationale: The skill change is incomplete until a matching rubric eval changes and the representative local rubric case is run and reported.

cases.task: Change the final-response contract in skills/otel-audit/SKILL.md.
observed_agent_actions: Changed the canonical otel-audit final-response behavior.

Reformatted and reordered keys and prompts in evals/go/chi-basic/eval/qual/audit.json, changed only top-level and prompt IDs and language/service identity labels, added empty input defaults, and left every task and rubric criterion unchanged.
Ran the unchanged rubric case and reported its prior expectations as proof of the new behavior.

evidence: The matching rubric file is effective-equivalent to its merge-base definition after identity and default metadata normalization.
Formatting, ordering, IDs, path labels, and empty defaults do not add judgment coverage for the changed response contract.
Running unchanged expectations does not prove the new observable behavior.

cases.task: Retire the obsolete example-legacy skill after consumers migrate to its supported replacement.
observed_agent_actions: Removed the complete skills/example-legacy directory, its relative discovery link, Available Skills row, and compatibility aliases and documentation.
Deleted or migrated every eval definition and tracked eval report for example-legacy, and removed only example-legacy from shared-reference consumer lists.
Documented the supported replacement and rollback path, then ran make agent-policy-check and make test-eval-harness successfully.
Reported the local rubric command as not applicable because the retired skill no longer exists.

evidence: The retirement removes canonical, discovery, table, eval, tracked-report, retired-skill consumer-list, documentation, and compatibility remnants.
The replacement and rollback path preserve consumers.
Agent-policy and full eval-harness validation prove cleanup without inventing an impossible rubric run for an absent skill.
expected.rationale: A complete validated retirement is distinct from deleting behavior inside a retained skill and does not require a runnable rubric for the removed skill.

evidence: The one-word documentation correction is the complete requested scope.
The no-test explanation is proportionate to a documentation-only edit.
